subject.title: RFC: Distributed Agent Runtime — separate control plane from agent compute

question: Should OpenClaw pursue this RFC as a core Gateway control-plane/per-agent-runtime architecture, narrow the active scope to subagent/ACP execution placement, or defer the distributed runtime direction for now?
rationale: The current code has partial Gateway, node, ACP, and subagent seams, but the full proposal changes process boundaries, secret isolation, session state, channel delivery, runtime config, and deployment operations.

options.title: Keep As Architecture Track
options.body: Use this issue to coordinate staged design for runtime protocol, trust boundary, session ownership, and embedded/local-split/distributed compatibility before code work.

options.title: Narrow To Execution Placement
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/82017 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/84758 as the active scope and leave the full Gateway/runtime split unresolved.

options.title: Defer Distributed Runtime
options.body: Park the RFC until security, setup, stability, and harness priorities justify a heavier orchestration layer.

recommendation.title: Keep As Architecture Track
recommendation.body: Use this issue to coordinate staged design for runtime protocol, trust boundary, session ownership, and embedded/local-split/distributed compatibility before code work.

likelyOwner.reason: The closed worker-runtime experiment and its follow-up comment provide the strongest current decision signal for the runtime isolation boundary.
